headline: Growth accelerates as Atlassian swings to GAAP profit
summary_short: Q4 FY2026 revenue rose 28% y/y to $1.77B as Cloud revenue grew 31% to $1.21B and RPO climbed 44% to $4.8B; Atlassian swung from a $28M GAAP operating loss a year ago to a $211M GAAP operating profit (12% margin).
summary_long: Atlassian's fiscal Q4 2026 revenue grew 28% y/y to $1.77B, Cloud up 31% to $1.21B, RPO up 44% to $4.8B, driven by enterprise AI adoption (Rovo, Teamwork Graph, MCP server past 1M monthly active users). GAAP operating income turned positive at $211M (12% margin) vs. a $28M loss a year ago; non-GAAP operating margin rose to 36% from 24%. Free cash flow was $475M. Cash fell to $1.24B (from $2.51B) after $1.8B of buybacks and a $1.23B acquisition; equity fell to $1.06B. Q1 FY2027 guide: revenue $1.705-1.715B, non-GAAP operating margin ~28.5%; FY2027 targets 13% revenue growth, 18% ARR growth.

drivers.explanation: CEO attributes the quarter to accelerating Cloud growth and AI-era demand for Atlassian's Teamwork Graph context, plus MCP server/Teamwork Graph CLI usage more than doubling quarter-over-quarter to 1M+ MAU.
Company attributes growth acceleration to continued Cloud migration and enterprise AI adoption of Rovo, Isolated Cloud, and AI governance controls launched during the quarter.
CFO ties RPO and ARR growth to enterprises deepening commitment to Atlassian's platform to deploy agents securely using the Teamwork Graph.
Total operating expenses grew 11.8% y/y ($1,178M to $1,317M) versus revenue growth of 27.6%, expanding operating leverage; CFO cites 'real operational discipline.'
Growth tracks non-GAAP operating income rising 89.5% y/y to $636M on revenue growth outpacing opex, plus a lower diluted share count (253.4M vs 265.7M).
Y/y decline reflects $1,800M of FY2026 share repurchases and $1,229M used for business combinations, partly offset by $1,353M of operating cash flow.
Decline driven by an accumulated deficit that widened to $6,105M alongside continued Class A share repurchases, only partly offset by additional paid-in capital growth.
